title: Print each name with a for loop
description:
Use for to print each name in the names list.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as printed_names(names), returning the exact multi-line string that a for loop printing each name on its own line would write to the screen (lines joined with '\n').
hints: A for loop like `for name in names: print(name)` writes one line per name, each ending in a newline.
'\n'.join(...) builds exactly that text - one item per line - without actually calling print().
expected_behavior: Returns the string that a for loop printing each name on its own line would produce, with lines separated by newline characters.
solution:
def printed_names(names):
    return '\n'.join(str(n) for n in names)

hidden_tests.label: four names printed one per line
empty list produces an empty string

explanation: '\n'.join() places a newline between each name, which is exactly the text a for loop calling print(name) on each item would send to the screen.
